# `'` `"` — Character and string literals

Single quotes hold exactly one character. Double quotes hold a string, which is a vector of any length.

```apl
⍴'a'               ⍝ ⍬ₓ
⍴"a"               ⍝ [1]ₓ
⍴"abc"             ⍝ [3]ₓ
⍴""                ⍝ [0]ₓ
```

The quote character is `'''`. An apostrophe needs no escaping inside a string. Double a double quote inside a string.

```apl
•ucs '''           ⍝ 39ₓ
≢"can't"           ⍝ 5ₓ
≢"say ""hi"""      ⍝ 8ₓ
```

Literals separated by spaces form a strand, which is one vector. Characters side by side form a string. Strings side by side form a vector of strings. So `"x" "y"` is two keys, and `'x' 'y'` is the one key `"xy"`.

```apl
'a' 'b'            ⍝ "ab"
≢"aa" "bb"         ⍝ 2ₓ
```

Results show strings in double quotes and characters in single quotes.

## Errors

- `SYNTAX`: single quotes around more or fewer than one character, an unclosed literal
